---
title: v3.1.2 — Unified Workflow Summaries and Validation Evidence
---

## Overview

Consolidate GitHub Actions validation results into one workflow summary per attempt, separating readable presentation from strict validation and retained evidence.

## Highlights

- Present macOS and Windows Rust, package, installer, downloader, Host simulation and checksum results side by side, with workspace and documentation test statistics, runner environment and proportional phase-duration bars.
- Tailor the shared summary to Branch, PR, Credentials and Publish workflows, preserving partial results and distinguishing failures, skipped checks, cancellations, timeouts and missing evidence.
- Retain strict Rust and installed Host evidence validation, release asset integrity, attestation and post-publication checks. Use functional artifact names and producer-attempt identifiers to avoid collisions and stale evidence on partial reruns.
- Keep Branch Rust and package validation parallel, make PR and publication stages follow adjacent job dependencies, and collect summary data without redundant cross-stage dependencies.
- Remove routine historical performance comparisons, compilation and process-cost investigations, redundant Markdown reports and obsolete charting code. Retain actual test evidence, failure diagnostics and validation timings.
- Extend automated regression tests for summary scope, failure handling, artifact identity, workflow dependencies and trusted credential boundaries.

The changes concern repository CI and release validation. Host simulations remain automated checks rather than live Codex or Claude Code execution.
